company_description: ClimbingPill is an elite climbing coaching platform founded by Ofer Blutrich, Israel's first 5.14c climber. It delivers structured, evidence-based training programs designed to break intermediate climbers through performance plateaus using 113 science-backed protocols that combine progressive training methodology with injury prevention.
company_mission: To give every motivated recreational climber access to elite-level, science-based coaching that turns plateaus into breakthroughs.
company_values: Evidence over tradition: every protocol is grounded in sports science, not gym lore
Structured progression: systematic training beats random sessions
Injury prevention as a core pillar, not an afterthought
Climber-first coaching: programs adapt to the individual, not the other way around
Transparency of method: climbers understand the why behind every session
company_positioning: The only climbing coaching program led by an elite 5.14c climber with a Master's degree in Physical Therapy, combining world-class climbing experience with clinical sports science to guarantee measurable grade breakthroughs.
company_differentiators: Founded and coached by Israel's first 5.14c climber with M.Sc in Physical Therapy
113 evidence-based training protocols — not generic fitness programming
Integrated injury prevention built into every training cycle
Specific, measurable outcome promise: V6 in 90 days
Black Diamond Pro athlete credibility backing the methodology
Bridges the gap between elite climbing knowledge and accessible recreational coaching

target_audience.description: Intermediate recreational climbers (typically V3-V5 range) who have hit a plateau and want to break through to V6 and beyond. They're motivated, train regularly, but lack a structured, science-based approach to progression. They're looking for expert guidance that combines training methodology with injury prevention.
segments: Plateau climbers: V3-V5 boulderers who train consistently but stopped progressing
Injury-cautious climbers: those who have been injured or want to train hard without breaking down
Structure seekers: climbers who know random gym sessions aren't working and want a real program
Progression-driven recreationals: not competing, but deeply motivated to reach the next grade

products_and_services.name: V6 Breakthrough Program
products_and_services.description: 90-day structured coaching program using evidence-based protocols to take climbers from the V3-V5 plateau to V6 and beyond

products_and_services.name: Climbing Assessment
products_and_services.description: Comprehensive evaluation of a climber's current strengths, weaknesses, and movement patterns to build a personalized training roadmap

products_and_services.name: Fingerboard Training Programs

products_and_services.name: Injury Prevention Protocols
products_and_services.description: Physiotherapy-informed protocols to keep climbers healthy through progressive training loads

brand_voice.tone: Confident, knowledgeable, and direct. Speaks as a coach who has done the hard climbs and studied the science — not as a salesperson. Warm but no-nonsense. Uses precise climbing language naturally.
personality_traits: Expert authority — speaks from lived elite climbing experience and clinical knowledge
Direct and actionable — gives clear guidance, not vague motivation
Science-grounded — references evidence and methodology, never hype
Passionate climber — genuine love for the sport comes through naturally
Approachable coach — elite credentials without elitist attitude
brand_voice.communication_style: Leads with specific outcomes and evidence. Uses climbing-specific terminology naturally (grades, send, project, flash). Explains the 'why' behind training decisions. Avoids generic fitness speak. Balances technical authority with coaching warmth.

spokesperson.name: Ofer Blutrich
spokesperson.title: Founder & Head Coach
spokesperson.bio: Ofer Blutrich is Israel's first 5.14c sport climber, a Black Diamond Pro team athlete, and holds a Master's degree in Physical Therapy. He built ClimbingPill to bridge the gap between elite climbing performance knowledge and accessible coaching for recreational climbers. His approach fuses decades of high-level climbing experience with evidence-based sports science and clinical physiotherapy expertise. Featured in Rock and Ice magazine.
credentials: Featured in Rock and Ice magazine
Certified physiotherapist specializing in climbing injuries
notable_achievements: Built ClimbingPill methodology combining PT and elite climbing

global_tone_rules: Always write as a coach-scientist: authoritative from experience, precise from education
Use climbing-specific language naturally — grades (V-scale, Yosemite Decimal), send, project, flash, crimp, sloper — never explain terms the target audience already knows
Lead with outcomes and evidence, not promises and hype
Be direct and specific: '113 protocols' is better than 'many methods'
Show the method, not just the result — readers should feel the structured thinking
Maintain warmth without softening authority — coach tone, not cheerleader tone
When referencing science, be concrete (name the principle or mechanism) rather than vaguely saying 'science-backed'
Write in active voice. Short sentences for impact. Longer sentences only when explaining methodology.
